The main takeaway from our work is that

the variability of the exposure of orally bioavailable drugs can be partitioned in interoccasion variability in relative bioavailability and interindividual variability in relative bioavailabity and in clearance.

the importance of exposure variability on the clinical outcome of an orally administered agent can be assessed more accurately when both IIV and IOV are accounted for in the exposure‐to‐response relationship.
